claims.text: AlCoFeNi can exist as an initially single ordered B2 phase at high temperature.
The initially single-phase alloy has a uniform microstructure.
Lower annealing temperatures promote decomposition of AlCoFeNi-based alloys into ordered B2 and disordered BCC phases.
The proposed lower-temperature annealing slows diffusion.
The proposed annealing produces nanoscale phase separation.
The length scale of B2+BCC decomposition depends on alloy composition and annealing temperature.
Phase decomposition produces nanometer- to sub-micrometer-scale precipitates preferentially along grain boundaries.
The grain-boundary precipitates produced by decomposition are incoherent.
Fine precipitates localized at grain boundaries generate stress concentrations during mechanical loading.
Fine grain-boundary precipitates lower grain-boundary cohesion.
The precipitate-induced stress concentration and loss of cohesion promote crack initiation and propagation.
Fine-scale grain-boundary decomposition causes a ductile-to-brittle transition in an initially single-phase HEA.
Conventional-alloy brittleness predominantly arises from elemental segregation or large brittle intermetallic grain-boundary phases.
The as-cast or solution-treated single-phase HEA has high toughness and a uniformly ductile microstructure.
Relative to the single-phase baseline, the annealed alloy will have lower fracture toughness.
Relative to the single-phase baseline, the annealed alloy will exhibit increased brittleness.
The proposed mechanism applies during moderate thermal excursions and standard mechanical loading rates but not at very high strain rates or temperatures far outside the treatment range.
The critical precipitate size and volume fraction for brittle transition vary with alloy composition.
